icons._strategy: PORT-DECISIONS decision 4: the six service SVGs ship as an INLINE SPRITE referenced from small html widgets. Mix with native/emoji icons so no page depends entirely on one source.
icons.sprite: child theme: assets/icons.svg (six 24x24 stroke icons, stroke-width 1.8, currentColor)

list_check._note: Native stand-in for .perk-list li::before and .spec-list li::before (a red disc with a knockout white check). FA Free Solid ships with Elementor.

watermarks._strategy: CSS PSEUDO-ELEMENTS in the child theme, not Elementor backgrounds. Decision 3 asked for background images + overlays; that route CANNOT place these - each watermark is a fixed-height box offset OUTSIDE its parent, and Elementor paints an element's own box, so the layer height is decoupled from both the element and the image 4:1 ratio. The cap's conditional 'watermark pseudo-elements' row therefore fired. build.py emits only the CLASS.
watermarks._assets: All four are 2000x500 viewBox wave graphics. WordPress blocks SVG uploads by default - ship them in the child theme (assets/), not the media library.
watermarks._pseudo_element: ::after, NOT ::before. Elementor already uses .e-con::before for a container background overlay and sets top/left/width/height/opacity on it, which over-constrains any watermark anchored with bottom/right and silently pins it to the top-left corner. .e-con::after is untouched by Elementor. The only ::before left is the .about band's second wave, which sets top AND left explicitly and so overrides Elementor outright.

about_top_left._note: Flipped. Elementor cannot transform a background - ship a pre-flipped 2-flip.svg.

watermarks._suppressed: .what-happens.about:before and :after are display:none - the About and Service Agreements pages each carry one .about section that must NOT get the wave pair.
watermarks._footer_padding_trap: Dropping the footer watermark means dropping section.footer_pad's 300px bottom too.

css_cap._policy: A hello-elementor CHILD THEME named mid-lakes, capped to this named rule list. Nothing else goes in it without a decision recorded in PORT-DECISIONS.md. No !important. One owner per property.
rules: .ml-h1 / .ml-h2 { font-size: clamp(...) } - the two fluid ramps
the six watermark pseudo-elements (.ml-wm-* / .ml-footer) - the cap's conditional row fired
.ml-rate-table (the whole table, one html widget, incl. the <620px card stacking)
.ml-nav ... .elementor-nav-menu { flex-wrap: nowrap } - Elementor ships `wrap` and offers no control; the prototype's .main-nav is nowrap
:focus-visible rings, incl. the band-by-band colour switch and forced-colors
.ml-header { backdrop-filter: blur(10px) } - Elementor's CSS Filters emit `filter:`, which would blur the header's own contents
prefers-reduced-motion: switches off the two transforms above
candidates: NONE OUTSTANDING. The two former candidates (.ml-card hover lift, the 3-stop overlays) were SHIPPED on the recommendation in PORT-DECISIONS so the pages could be finished. Both are one rule each, marked [cap CANDIDATE] in mid-lakes.css, and removable without touching a single build.py - they still want a yes/no.
css_cap._class_landing: build.py emits _css_classes for widgets and css_classes for containers. A widget class lands on the WRAPPER (.elementor-widget-button), so a button rule must be .ml-btn .elementor-button, never .ml-btn.
css_cap._specificity: Elementor's per-element rule is 4 classes (0,4,0); a bare class is (0,2,0). Elementor always wins. Do not fight it - omit the property from build.py when the child theme owns it.
css_cap._size: 134 declarations. 73% of them are two components: the rate table (50) and the watermarks (49). The remaining ~35 are irreducible - each is a property Elementor has no control for. See the audit in the session notes: the watermarks are decoration and are the one line item worth re-deciding on cost.
css_cap._pseudo_elements: ::after, not ::before. Elementor already uses .e-con::before for a container background overlay and sets top/left/width/height/opacity on it, silently pinning any bottom/right-anchored layer to the top-left corner.
